'''David Milstein''' ({{Langx|he|דוד מילשטין}}; born June 4, 1947) is an Israeli chemist studying [[homogeneous catalysis]]. In 2026, he was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]].

==Education and early life==
Milstein was born in 1947 in Ulm, Germany where his family took refuge after being displaced during the [[Holocaust]]. With his family, he immigrated  to the newly founded state of Israel at the age of two. Milstein was first fascinated by chemistry when attending high school in the town of [[Rehovot]] where “an enthusiastic, old-fashioned chemistry teacher who didn’t care much about orbitals” inspired him “with vivid, thought-provoking experiments”.<ref>The Skeptical Chymist (http://blogs.nature.com/thescepticalchymist/2008/09/reactions_david_milstein.html)</ref>
Pursuing his interest, Milstein received B.Sc., M.Sc., and Ph.D. degrees in chemistry from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.{{when|date=April 2019}}

==Career and research==
Milstein carried out [[postdoctoral research]] at the University of Iowa and at Colorado State University with [[John Kenneth Stille]], where he performed key research leading up to the [[Stille reaction]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Milstein | first1 = D. | last2 = Stille | first2 = J. K. | year = 1978 | title =A general, selective, and facile method for ketone synthesis from acid chlorides and organotin compounds catalyzed by palladium| journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc. | volume = 100 | issue = 11| pages = 3636–3638 | doi = 10.1021/ja00479a077 | bibcode = 1978JAChS.100.3636M }}</ref> This reaction remains highly topical. In 1979 at the conclusion of his postdoc, Milstein joined [[DuPont Central Research]] & Development in Wilmington, Delaware, where he became a group leader in the area of homogeneous catalysis. In 1987, he took position at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], where he is now the Israel Matz Professorial Chair of [[Organic Chemistry]].

===Independent research===
Milstein's research has mainly focused on complexes of groups 8, 9, and 10 transition-metal complexes.  A hallmark of his research is the use of pincer ligands, particularly those with substituents that absorb or release hydrogen.

[[File:MilsteinCat.svg|thumb|right|380 px|Reaction of H<sub>2</sub> with a Milstein catalyst.]]

In early independent research, he examined the activation of C-C, C-H, C-F, N-H, and O-H bonds.[http://apps.isiknowledge.com/summary.do?qid=1&product=WOS&SID=1ClAmHdB%40B2PO6AKI3D&search_mode=GeneralSearch]{{Dead link|date=November 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. In one case, he described insertion of rhodium into a C-C bond using a pincer-type substrate.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gozin | first1 = M. | last2 = Weisman | first2 = A. | last3 = Ben-David | first3 = Y. | last4 = Milstein | first4 = D. | year = 1993 | title = Activation of a carbon–carbon bond in solution by transition-metal insertion | journal = Nature | volume = 364 | issue = 6439| pages = 699–701 | doi=10.1038/364699a0| bibcode = 1993Natur.364..699G | s2cid = 4314638 }}</ref> This paper established a general strategy for C-C activation in homogeneous systems.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gozin | first1 = M. | last2 = Aizenberg | first2 = M. | last3 = Liou | first3 = S.-Y. | last4 = Weisman | first4 = A. | last5 = Ben-David | first5 = Y. | last6 = Milstein | first6 = D. | year = 1994 | title = Transfer of methylene groups promoted by metal complexation | journal = Nature | volume = 370 | issue = 6484| pages = 42–44 | doi=10.1038/370042a0| bibcode = 1994Natur.370...42G | s2cid = 4253452 }}The Fall of the C-C Bond http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v364/n6439/abs/364676a0.html</ref> Related research focused on other strong bonds to carbon, e.g. the C-F bond.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Aizenberg | first1 = M. | last2 = Milstein | first2 = D. | year = 1994 | title = Catalytic activation of carbon-fluorine bonds by a soluble transition metal complex | journal = Science | volume = 265 | issue = 5170| pages = 359–361 | doi=10.1126/science.265.5170.359 | pmid=17838035| bibcode = 1994Sci...265..359A | s2cid = 20245305 }}</ref> In other research at the early stages in his independent career, he examined the then rare [[oxidative addition]] of N-H and O-H.<ref>Zhang et al. http://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja059914h</ref>

Milstein achieved acclaim for the discovery of [[pincer complex]]es that catalyze dehydrogenation reactions concomitant with condensations.  In one breakthrough, [[amides]] are generated by  dehydrocoupling of a mixture of [[alcohols]] and [[amines]]:<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gunanathan | first1 = C. | last2 = Ben-David | first2 = Y. | last3 = Milstein | first3 = D. | year = 2007 | title = Direct synthesis of amides from alcohols and amines with liberation of H2 | journal = Science | volume = 317 | issue = 5839| pages = 790–792 | doi=10.1126/science.1145295 | pmid=17690291| bibcode = 2007Sci...317..790G | s2cid = 43671648 }}</ref> 
: RCH<sub>2</sub>OH  +  R'NH<sub>2</sub>  →   RC(O)NHR'  +  2 H<sub>2</sub>  
This discovery was selected by ''Science'' magazine as one of the top ten breakthroughs of 2007. The reaction has been praised for its selectivity and mildness. H<sub>2</sub> gas is the only by-product.<ref>Breakthrough of the Year http://www.sciencemag.org/cgi/content/full/318/5858/1844a</ref>
Related processes allow the synthesis of esters from alcohols:<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zhang | first1 = J. | last2 = Leitus | first2 = G. | last3 = Ben-David | first3 = Y. | last4 = Milstein | first4 = D. | year = 2005 | title = Facile conversion of alcohols into esters and dihydrogen catalyzed by new ruthenium complexes | journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc. | volume = 127 | issue = 31| pages = 10840–10841 | doi=10.1021/ja052862b| pmid = 16076184 | bibcode = 2005JAChS.12710840Z }}</ref>
: 2 RCH<sub>2</sub>OH   →   RC(O)OR  +  2 H<sub>2</sub>

In a quite different direction, Milstein and his co-workers described a solution-phase reaction scheme for water splitting.  In this system, he devised ruthenium catalysts to promote the evolution of hydrogen and oxygen in consecutive thermal- and light-driven steps.  The process embodied a new light-driven water splitting strategy that does not require a sacrificial chemical in the process.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Kohl | first1 = S. W. | last2 = Weiner | first2 = L. | last3 = Schwartsburd | first3 = L. | last4 = Konstantinovski | first4 = L. | last5 = Shimon | first5 = L. J. W. | last6 = Ben-David | first6 = Y. | last7 = Iron | first7 = M. A. | last8 = Milstein | first8 = D. | year = 2009 | title = Consecutive thermal H2 and light-induced O2 evolution from water promoted by a metal complex | journal = Science | volume = 324 | issue = 5923| pages = 74–77 | doi=10.1126/science.1168600 | pmid=19342584| bibcode = 2009Sci...324...74K | s2cid = 45998269 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Poverenov | first1 = E. | last2 = Efremenko | first2 = I. | last3 = Frenkel | first3 = A. I. | last4 = Ben-David | first4 = Y. | last5 = Shimon | first5 = L. J. W. | last6 = Leitus | first6 = G. | last7 = Konstantinovski | first7 = L. | last8 = Martin | first8 = J. M. L. | last9 = Milstein | first9 = D. | year = 2008 | title = Evidence for a terminal Pt(IV)-oxo complex exhibiting diverse reactivity | journal = Nature | volume = 455 | issue = 7216| pages = 1093–1096 | doi=10.1038/nature07356| bibcode = 2008Natur.455.1093P | s2cid = 4413632 }}</ref><ref>New way to split water https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2009/04/090406102555.htm</ref>

*	The 2007 [[American Chemical Society]] Award in Organometallic Chemistry

*	The [[Paolo Chini]] Memorial Award 1999 (awarded by the Italian Chemical Society)

==Personal life==
Son of Musia and Abraham and younger brother of Lea, Milstein married to Adi Milstein in 1971, with whom he has three children: Nofit (b. 1972), Oren (b. 1976, cofounder of [[StemRad]]), and Abraham (b. 1983).  He resides in the town of Rehovot in Israel.
